messages:
neha: Heads up — after the CUDA 12.2 + driver 535.113 rollout to the staging GPU nodepools, ~18/120 A100 nodes booted with MIG profiles missing. Scheduler failing allocations for dedicated pools. Anyone seen profiles vanish like this?
alex: Which pool/region?
neha: us-east1-staging-gpu, A100-SXM nodes. Affected are spread across two racks.
sam: Can you paste the nvidia-smi output you saw?
neha: Ran: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,gpu_uuid,mig.mode.current --format=csv`
```
Name, GPU UUID, MIG Mode
A100-SXM-40GB, GPU-b1f2a8e4-..., disabled
A100-SXM-40GB, GPU-b1f2a8f5-..., disabled
```
chris: That matches a weird case I hit last month after pushing 535.110 -> 535.113: MIG control plane failed to restore on some SKUs. Any dmesg or nvml logs?
neha: dmesg shows: `nvidia-mig: failed to restore profile: operation not supported` and a handful of `NVRM: Xid (79): GPU exception` entries. Also saw `nvmlDeviceGetGpuInstanceById: GPU_IS_LOST`.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-045 (severity: high)
maria: Do UUIDs look different? Our mig-config controller matches by GPU UUID; if those shift the controller won't reapply.
neha: Good call — we see expected UUIDs in the config map vs node output mismatch for 9 of the affected cards. Example: config expected `GPU-9a2...` but `nvidia-smi` reports `GPU-b1f2...`.
alex: Could be NVidia driver changed how UUIDs are reported after kernel module load order. What kernel version are the nodes on?
neha: Kernel v5.19.12 (no change), driver 535.113 (rolled via daemonset). `modinfo nvidia | grep version` -> `version: 535.113`
sam: Mitigation suggestions: 1) taint affected nodes `kubectl taint nodes <node> gpu-mig-broken=true:NoSchedule` 2) rollback driver on a small batch to 535.101 and test MIG restore 3) run a UUID-mapping script to update the controller config if safe 4) add preflight `nvidia-smi mig -lgi` check to upgrade pipeline.
chris: Reconfiguring MIG in-place requires correct NVML state. You can try `nvidia-smi mig -cgi <cfg>` to restore profiles, but if NVML says GPU_IS_LOST you'll need driver rollback + reboot. Also note some combos of CUDA/toolkit + driver change NVML semantics.
neha: Tried `nvidia-smi mig -cgi 0,6,13` — returns `ERROR: Cannot change MIG configuration: NVML_ERROR_GPU_IS_LOST` on half of the nodes. On others the command worked and profiles came back.
maria: Immediate business impact: ~9% capacity loss in staging dedicated pools; if we shift workloads to other regions cost goes up ~14% for the week. We should avoid full rollout until root cause fixed.
alex: Opening a formal NVIDIA ticket CNTRL-12345 and attached a full `nvidia-bug-report` + dmesg. They asked for the bug report and a node-accesser for repro.
ops-bot: PagerDuty alert acknowledged by oncall
sam: Operational plan I'm starting: 1) mark affected nodes and un-schedule new rollouts 2) pick 3 nodes for driver rollback and test MIG reapply 3) if rollback fixes, run a targeted rollback + reconverge 4) add post-upgrade `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=mig.mode.current --format=csv` gating step to pipeline 5) update mig-config controller to tolerate UUID drift (fallback by PCI slot id)
neha: I'll label the affected nodes `gpu-mig=broken` and add to the incident doc. Also adding a note to the rollout runbook to hold upgrades for A100-SXM until we get a vendor confirmation.
chris: If we need a faster fix, we can temporarily allow the controller to match by `pci.bus` id, but that has fragility during reboots. Prefer vendor fix or rollback.
maria: Can we estimate impact on upcoming Dedicated commitments? Ops, please check whether any committed capacity is impacted — if so we need to notify customer success.
alex: Copying commit-owner; will run capacity check.
neha: Quick test result: rollback on node us-east1-std-12 returned profiles after reboot and `nvidia-smi mig -lgi` lists the expected instances. I'll run mapping script next to see if we can safely patch the config map for the remaining nodes.
sam: Note for follow-up: add an automated MIG verification step in cluster-upgrade job and a post-rollout 30m health check that fails the job if any `NVML_ERROR_GPU_IS_LOST` occurs.
ops-bot: INC-2026-045 updated — runbook link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-045
neha: Thanks — I'm going to pause the remaining CUDA/driver rollouts and coordinate rollback on a narrow blast radius. Will post updates here after mapping script runs.
sam: I'll run the mapping and validate on a 20% sample before we untaint nodes. Leaving notes for morning handoff.
